hypothesis: Distractor-aware data and explicit refusal/confirmation training have distinguishable main and interaction effects on exact tool selection while eliminating unsafe calls, and at least one arm dominates the 45M incumbent's risk/coverage curve.

comparison.experimental_unit: one independently trained model seed evaluated on one frozen prompt
comparison.replicate_unit: one independent training seed, not repeated decoding from one checkpoint

randomization.method: seeded permutation of arm order within each seed block and prompt order within evaluation slices

metrics.gate: every recipe must overfit the 1-10 KB repeated fixture before a full run
selected arm improves paired tool-selection exactness over the 45M incumbent
selected arm beats the incumbent on the sealed risk/coverage frontier at nonzero coverage
quantized candidate retains the selected full-precision safety and exactness decision

resource_envelope.stop_rule: Stop an arm on tiny-overfit failure or unsafe dev actions; if no arm passes dev, reject 45M and advance to the 1.7B class without opening sealed V2.

protocol_history.reason: The first tiny-overfit invocation produced no model result because unconstrained Flax 0.10.4 called jax.api_util.debug_info, an API absent from the JAX 0.4.38 required by JAX-Metal. Version 2 pins Flax 0.10.2; data, recipes, seeds, gates, and resource caps are unchanged.

The second tiny-overfit invocation produced no model result because JAX-Metal on the Apple M5 Pro could not legalize Needle's batched-attention mhlo.dot_general before step 1. Version 3 freezes the same float32 reference path on CPU with zero GPU-hours; model math, data, recipes, seeds, gates, and resource caps are unchanged.

The first CPU tiny invocation exposed unequal optimizer steps because the 1 KB file rule produced two plain JSONL rows and one distractor row. It also showed that the eight-tool positive example hit the 1024-token cap. Version 4 freezes one padded row and 200 equal steps for every recipe, and uses Needle's advertised target-plus-four retrieval width for distractor training. No full factorial or sealed result was produced.

All four equalized tiny optimizations reached loss 0.0001, then the decoding harness stopped before scoring because tiny training rows use answers while evaluation rows use expected_tool. Version 5 normalizes the two frozen representations without changing adapters, data, recipes, seeds, thresholds, or gates.

All four tiny adapters scored 100% exact after normalization, but the receipt writer used NumPy-free system Python and could not unpickle adapter metadata. Version 6 runs decisions under the frozen experiment interpreter; no training, decoding, threshold, or result changed.

The first full arm was stopped before a checkpoint after 16/210 steps because measured CPU step time projected the 12-run factorial beyond the frozen three-hour stage cap. Version 7 retains all 216 examples, optimizer settings, factors, seeds, and gates but freezes seven epochs (98 steps per run), projected inside the measured host budget. No dev or sealed output was seen.
